title: Google login
summary: Apply Spring OAuth2 login to Google, then associate the validated external identity with a local account.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: OAuth2 in Spring Boot | How to Add Google Login in Spring Boot | Complete Tutorial

richText: Google login uses the OAuth2 client capability described in the OAuth2 lesson.
The Spring application is the login client.
A Google OAuth client registration supplies the client ID and client secret.
The registration's allowed redirect URI must match Spring's callback URI exactly.

example.title: Configure Google login for browser sessions
description: Each example is a separate project. All required application files appear in the tabs.
The Google registration includes the exact callback URI for the application.
The default local callback assumes the application runs on port `8080`.
explanation: Spring redirects the browser to Google and saves the authorization request.
Google returns an authorization code to `/login/oauth2/code/google`.
Spring checks the returned state and exchanges the code for tokens.
The `openid` scope makes Spring validate an ID token and create an `OidcUser`.
Successful login establishes a session for later application requests.
CSRF protection remains enabled for state-changing requests.
A controller can obtain the logged-in principal with `@AuthenticationPrincipal OidcUser user`.
The provider client secret stays on the server.

files.name: src/main/resources/application.yml
files.code:
spring:
  security:
    oauth2:
      client:
        registration:
          google:
            client-id: ${GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID}
            client-secret: ${GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET}
            scope:
              - openid
              - profile
              - email
